comments.author: dougmassay
comments.body:
That typically only happens if the warning message that splitting files with fragment urls with missing targets might cause problems is ignored. The warning message was specifically added because there are certain conditions that can't be properly accommodated by Sigil's splitting routines. Namely: if there is no element with an id of "anchor1" in "this_file.xhtml" the warning will pop. If the warnin g is ignored, paths will not be correctly updated.

If you don't get a warning message in the situations where this can occur, then you might be using an older version of Sigil that doesn't give the warning.

comments.author: gennaios
comments.body:
I am using the newest version of Sigil and have kept up with versions. It’s been happening perhaps most of the time in the last year, perhaps not as long, perhaps longer.

I get no warning or error message, and all anchors exist. For example, a file may have dozens of footnotes at the end, all of them correct, and anchors are not rewritten after the split. Now, for any file I do split, I check first for such anchors and edit them to `… href=“#…”`, removing the file name, and all behaves as intended.

comments.author: dougmassay
comments.body: We'd love to have a reproduceable sample where existing valid/working urls aren't being properly updated when splitting (without being warned of the possibility beforehand). This is the first such report since the the warning message was added. If something is falling through the cracks, we'd love to fix it. But we have to be able reproduce it first.

comments.author: kevinhendricks
comments.body:
To be clear, is this what you are describing?

you have a single xhtml  say with filename "file1.xhtml" and it has an internal link to a target "#here" in that same file but the href for the anchor is currently written as "file1.xhtml#here" instead of just "#here".

Then when you split this file between the href anchor and the link target, the href does not get properly updated.  

Is that what you are saying?

comments.author: kevinhendricks
comments.body:
Also from reading the href <a> html spec, when a href is internal to that file, only a fragment identifier is used, not the name of the file (since it is in the same file).

 hrefs like that are technically not correct, but may still work.  So it is a good idea to search for the name of the file inside the file correcting any improperly written local hrefs, before attempting any split.

If this is what is going on we should be able to include tests for this in our warning for splitting.

comments.author: gennaios
comments.body:
Hello Kevin,

Yes that is correct, anchors internal to the file are named with the file name as you cited. It’s happened perhaps at least 4 or 5 times, always commercial ePubs, often academic titles. Some publishers perhaps have a habit of writing their epubs as such, with all internal files being as such. Thus it would be nice and ideal to automatically correct and handle such cases.

Not in front of a computer but I will try to create a reproducible case unless you think such would happen as such since such a case isn’t currently handled.
